news.title: Asian Football Confederation postpones the 2027 Asian Cup because of conflict in the Middle East
news.lede: The Asian Football Confederation has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup by almost a year because of the conflict in the Middle East and security concerns in Saudi Arabia. The AFC issued a statement Tuesday saying that, after extensive consultations with Saudi organizers, it had decided to push the tournament kickoff back from Jan. 7 to Dec. The organizing committee “approved rescheduling the flagship national team tournament in light of the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions,” the AFC said in a statement. The new dates — Dec. 23, 2027 to Jan. 21, 2028 — will be submitted to FIFA for approval.

news.title: Auckland United in contention for place at first FIFA Women’s Club World Cup
news.lede: FIFA have confirmed the United States will host the inaugural Women’s Club World Cup in January 2028, with Auckland United among the contenders for Oceania’s place at the global event. The new competition will feature 19 clubs from FIFA’s six continental confederations, with matches scheduled between January 5-30, 2028. FIFA have also revealed the qualification criteria and confirmed seven clubs have already secured places in the tournament. They are Arsenal (England), Barcelona (Spain), Club América (Mexico), Gotham FC (United States), Naegohyang (DPR Korea), Corinthians (Brazil) and Wuhan Jiangda (China PR).

news.title: Fifa to share documents on World Cup sell-off plans with council members
news.lede: Viewings to take place at Fifa’s headquarters in Zurich. No direct response to Uefa’s questions on governance. Fifa will grant its council members access to documents regarding the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme but has not responded directly to more than 50 questions from Uefa about its governance and recent scandals. In a letter sent to the Fifa Council by Mattias Grafström, the governing body’s secretary general, members were told material relating to FFE will be released for them to view in person at Fifa’s headquarters in Zurich.
